what: A sign-in screen and a dashboard, 200px apart, joined by an arrow bound from the Continue button to the second screen.
why: Pins two things at once: navigation detection (a bound cross-screen arrow must be reported as a flow naming the control that triggers it), and what undeclared controls infer to. The inputs and the checkbox carry no declared role on purpose — this fixture is the guard on the inference path, so it is expected to score 3 inferred, not 0.
notes: The 3 inferred are `email` and `password` (white boxes read as input?) and `remember` (a 24px square reads as checkbox?).

The "Remember me" text is folded into the checkbox rather than listed separately — a tickbox and its words are one control to a reader. That is why 15 elements produce 13 components: the arrow and the absorbed label are both accounted for.
